A player-facing copy of this entry lives in the public Rules Reference compendium as @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.cd91fc7339974dcd]{Diablerie}; this ST-only copy exists only because other Storyteller-facing docs already link to it directly.

Diablerie (the Amaranth) is the act of devouring another vampire's blood and soul together. It is the most feared crime in Kindred society, sparking blood hunts on mere suspicion, yet it remains tempting because it can let the diablerist climb closer to Caine.

Committing Diablerie

  1. Incapacitate the target. The victim must be physically immobilized before diablerie can begin.
  2. Drain blood. The diablerist automatically drains one Blood Trait per turn; no challenge is required for this stage.
  3. Drain health levels. The diablerist strips away health levels until the victim falls into torpor. The victim resists with a Physical Challenge per health level using only stamina-related Traits and cannot harm the diablerist in the process; if the diablerist can no longer match the victim's Physical Traits, she falls away and the victim may die or escape. While draining, the diablerist cannot be targeted by Mental or Social Challenges, but she also cannot defend herself — outside attacks against her succeed automatically.
  4. Drain the Essence (the soul). Once the victim is drained of blood and in torpor, the diablerist attempts a Physical Challenge to seize the departing soul; the victim's side of this challenge is treated as three Traits up. The diablerist may keep trying until she can no longer match the victim's Traits — success absorbs the soul, ultimate failure lets it escape to the afterlife.

Others may help incapacitate or drain a victim, but only one Kindred can claim the final Essence. A diablerist who wants to stop after Stage Three must spend a Willpower Trait and win a Static Mental Challenge (difficulty three Traits), or her hunger drives her to finish the act regardless.

Only vampires can be diablerized. Mortals, ghosts, and other supernatural beings have no torpor state for a soul to linger in — their souls flee the instant the body dies, so they can be killed or drained of blood but never diablerized.

Rewards

  • On success, the diablerist is overcome with euphoria and must immediately check to resist frenzy.
  • If the victim was of a lower generation (more potent blood) than the diablerist, the diablerist's own generation improves by one step, granting the benefits of the new generation immediately.
  • A victim five or more generations more potent may grant more than one generational step, at the Storyteller's discretion.
  • The diablerist gains two extra Experience Traits at the end of the session.
  • A sufficiently powerful victim may grant a temporary surge in the diablerist's Disciplines for the remainder of the scene, entirely at Narrator discretion.

Perils

  • A character who follows Humanity automatically loses at least one Humanity Trait for committing diablerie (more for an especially foul act), with no test or appeal; characters on a Path lose a Path Trait unless that Path condones the act.
  • Aura Perception can detect diablerie as black veins running through a vampire's aura for up to three months after the act.
  • The Thaumaturgy power A Taste for Blood can detect a history of diablerie regardless of how long ago it occurred.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} princes treat discovered diablerists with an immediate blood hunt, sometimes extended to other cities, and hunters are often permitted (or quietly allowed) to diablerize the criminal themselves.
  • Some legends hold that a diablerist may pick up mannerisms of an especially strong-willed or much-lower-generation victim, a detail sharp-eyed Storytellers can use against habitual diablerists.
